# Style guide

<p className="canopy-lead">Every Canopy page is drawn from one small set of styles: two families, two weights, eleven text styles, a palette from your theme, and a few shapes and steps of space. Components use nothing else, so a change you make in `canopy.yml` or in a token restyles every one of them.</p>

This page draws each style with the stylesheet your site ships, in its theme, so what you see is what your pages get. Its numbers are read from the page as it renders.

## Type

Canopy sets type as a magazine does: a sans for headlines and the interface, a serif for reading.

### Families

<StyleGuide.Families />

### Weights

Two weights, and only two: **bold (700)** for headings, labels, a card's title and emphasis, and regular (400) for everything else. Hierarchy comes from size and color, not from weights in between.

### Text styles

Every piece of text on a page is one of these. Headings, paragraphs and lists you write in Markdown take them on their own; components take them from the stylesheet.

<StyleGuide.TypeStyles />

Use them in your own markup with their classes:

| Style            | Class                    | Size token                           |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| Display          | `canopy-type-display`    | `--canopy-text-display`              |
| Title            | `canopy-type-title`      | `--canopy-text-title`                |
| Heading 2        | `canopy-type-h2`         | `--canopy-text-2xl`                  |
| Heading 3        | `canopy-type-h3`         | `--canopy-text-xl`                   |
| Heading 4 to 6   | `canopy-type-h4`         | `--canopy-text-lg`                   |
| Lede             | `canopy-type-lede`       | `--canopy-text-lede`                 |
| Body             | `canopy-type-body`       | `--canopy-text-body`                 |
| Interface        | `canopy-type-ui`         | `--canopy-text-md`                   |
| Interface, small | `canopy-type-ui-sm`      | `--canopy-text-sm`                   |
| Label            | `canopy-type-label`      | `--canopy-text-label`                |
| Code             | `canopy-type-code`       | `--canopy-text-code`                 |

```mdx
<p className="canopy-type-label">Featured</p>
<p className="canopy-type-lede">Prints and drawings from three collections.</p>
```

A class sets the look only. Use the element that says what the text is, such as a heading for a heading, so the page's outline stays right.

## Color

Colors come from your theme (`accentColor`, `grayColor` and `appearance` in `canopy.yml`). Canopy holds each pair of text and ground at 4.5:1 or more, and each control's edge and focus ring at 3:1, for every palette, in light and dark.

### Fills

<StyleGuide.Swatches group="fills" />

### Surfaces and edges

Panels are solid fills, not outlines; cards are lifted off the page with a hairline and a soft shadow.

<StyleGuide.Swatches group="surfaces" />

### Black

A band and a code block are black in both appearances.

<StyleGuide.Swatches group="black" />

## Shape

Corners nest: what sits inside a rounded thing takes a smaller step. Search fields and round controls are pills.

<StyleGuide.Shapes />

Keyboard focus is always a ring in the accent, standing off the element so the page shows between, as above.

## Space

Space steps on the golden ratio from the page's `1rem`. The more closely two things belong together, the smaller the step between them; a container's inset is a step larger than the gap between what it holds.

<StyleGuide.Spacing />
